drug_class: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) agonist — a topical anti-inflammatory cream
purpose: Tapinarof is a prescription cream used to treat plaque psoriasis in adults and atopic dermatitis (eczema) in patients 2 years and older. It helps calm the red, itchy, scaly patches on your skin. It is applied directly to the affected areas of the skin.
how_it_works: Tapinarof works by activating a specific protein in your skin cells called the aryl hydrocarbon receptor. When activated, this helps reduce inflammation and calm the overactive immune response that causes your skin to become red, scaly, and itchy. Think of it like a dimmer switch that turns down the inflammation in your skin without using steroids.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include folliculitis (small pimple-like bumps around hair follicles), itching or burning at the application site, and skin reactions where you apply the cream. Some people may also experience a common cold or headache. These side effects are usually mild.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you develop severe skin reactions or signs of infection at the application site. Avoid getting the cream in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. It is not known if this medication is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding, so talk to your doctor first. Keep this medication out of reach of children and store it at room temperature.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of the cream to the affected skin areas once a day. Rub it in gently until it disappears into the skin. Only apply it to the areas of skin that are bothered by your condition — do not apply it to normal healthy skin. Wash your hands after applying unless you are treating your hands.
